notes: C1 literally requires >=140 systolic AND >90 diastolic; no pilot case depends on this wording (flag for expert review).

criteria.text: Uncontrolled hypertension (>=140 systolic and >90 diastolic) despite active management
criteria.span: Diagnosis of uncontrolled hypertension (≥ 140 mm Hg systolic blood pressure and > 90 mm Hg diastolic blood pressure) despite active management by a clinician with primary responsibility for blood pressure management

criteria.text: Diagnosed by ambulatory or serial home blood pressure monitoring
criteria.span: Uncontrolled hypertension diagnosed using either ambulatory blood pressure monitoring or serial home blood pressure readings

criteria.text: Lifestyle changes and stable maximally tolerated GDMT with adherence assessment for at least 6 weeks
criteria.span: On lifestyle modifications and stable doses of maximally tolerated guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), with assessment of adherence to the prescribed regimen, for at least six weeks before referral for RDN

criteria.text: Screened for primary aldosteronism, OSA, and drug/alcohol-induced hypertension
criteria.span: At a minimum, patients must be screened for primary aldosteronism, obstructive sleep apnea, and drug or alcohol induced hypertension before referral to RDN

criteria.text: No contraindications per the device's FDA labeling
criteria.span: The patient has no contraindications to RDN, consistent with the FDA labeling of the device used

criteria.text: Coordinated management for at least 6 months with at least 3 encounters, at most 2 virtual
criteria.span: The primary clinicians must coordinate management of the patient for a minimum of six months before referral for RDN, during which the patient had at least three encounters, with no more than two of the three encounters being virtual

criteria.text: Only within a CMS-approved CED study
criteria.span: RDN is not covered for patients outside of a CMS-approved study

criteria.text: Operator completed at least five proctored RDN cases with each device used
criteria.span: must complete at least five proctored RDN cases with each approved device used in their practice

cases.vignette: 62-year-old woman with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring showing daytime average 158/96 mm Hg. On lifestyle modification and stable maximally tolerated doses of four antihypertensives (including a diuretic and spironolactone) for 4 months, with adherence confirmed by pharmacy refill records and pill counts. Screening was negative for primary aldosteronism (normal aldosterone-renin ratio), obstructive sleep apnea (home sleep test), and drug- or alcohol-induced hypertension. Her primary care physician has co-managed her blood pressure for 14 months with five encounters, four in person. The planned FDA market-authorized RDN device will be used per its labeled indication. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study. The operator is an interventional cardiologist with active endovascular experience who completed five proctored cases with this device; the facility runs a hypertension program with a hypertension navigator and specialist access, has CT angiography, and a cardiac catheterization lab. Referral is by the primary care physician who manages the patient's hypertension longitudinally. Renal CT angiography shows anatomy suitable for RDN and there are no contraindications in the device labeling. No prior RDN.
